title: But what is a neural network? | Deep learning chapter 1
beats: A sloppy low-res 3: your brain reads it effortlessly despite wildly different pixels
Flip: write a program to do this and the task goes from trivial to daunting
Promise: structure now, learning next video; plain-vanilla network only, it will fall short of some hopes
A neuron is just a thing holding a number between 0 and 1
784 input neurons = pixel grayscale; activation = lit-up brightness
Output layer of 10 digits; hidden layers left as a giant question mark
Two hidden layers of 16 admitted to be arbitrary, chosen to fit the motivation and the screen
Activations cascade layer to layer; shows trained network lighting up, brightest output is the guess
Why expect layers to work? You recognise a 9 as loop + line, 8 as two loops
Hope: penultimate layer = subcomponents; admits this just kicks the problem down the road
Loops break into edges; second layer = little edges; flagged as a hope to revisit after training
Layers of abstraction also fit speech: sounds to syllables to words to phrases
Picture yourself designing the mechanism: what dials and knobs should one edge-detector neuron have?
Weights on each connection; weighted sum; weights drawn as green/red pixel grid
Zero weights except a region sums that region; negative surround makes an edge detector
Squish sum into 0-1 with sigmoid/logistic curve
Bias: want activity only when sum exceeds 10, so add -10 before squishing
One neuron, then a whole layer: 784x16 weights + 16 biases, then ~13,000 knobs total
Learning = finding a valid setting for all those numbers
Thought experiment: set all 13,000 by hand; why understanding weights beats black box
Cumbersome function compacted into sigmoid(Wa+b) as matrix-vector product
Pointer to linear algebra series chapter 3; compact form makes code simpler and faster
Refine: a neuron is really a function; whole network is a function 784 to 10
Its complexity is reassuring given the task; how it learns is next video
Subscribe joke about YouTube's recommender neural networks; Patreon
Lisha Li: sigmoid is old school; ReLU = max(0,a) trains better for deep nets

theory: The video motivates structure by reverse-engineering a hope: it asks what a layered network would ideally do (edges -> loops -> digits) before introducing any mechanism, so weights and bias arrive as answers to a design question the viewer already holds. Definitions start deliberately thin and are explicitly upgraded later, which keeps symbol cost near zero until the payoff.
velocity: Orchestrator: before introducing a mechanism, pose a 'what would we hope each part does' design question and let the learner propose decompositions
Scene builder: render parameters as a spatial grid on the input (green/red weight pixels) so abstract numbers inherit the input's geometry
Learner model: track which definitions are provisional and schedule an explicit 'upgrade' beat (holds a number -> is a function)
Voice: flag hopeful mechanisms as hypotheses to verify, then return to them, building trust via honest-caveat
Evals: check notation appears only after its concept has been used concretely at least once
quote: all I want you to think about is a thing that holds a number
